Returned to Selhurst Park to become Palace's all-time Premier League top scorer with 68 goals, almost single-handedly securing their top-flight survival year after year.
Wore shirt #11, talismanic winger renowned for ankle-breaking stepovers, winning fouls, and emotional fiery passion.
Iconic / Primary Club: Crystal Palace

name: Benni McCarthy
bonusClues: Won the 2004 Champions League with Porto under José Mourinho before moving to Ewood Park for £2.5 million in 2006.
Finished as the second-highest scorer in the Premier League in 2006-07 with 18 league goals (behind only Didier Drogba).
Wore shirt #10, lethal penalty-box assassin celebrated for instinctive first-time finishes and acrobatic celebrations.
Iconic / Primary Club: Blackburn Rovers

name: Stiliyan Petrov
bonusClues: Won four Scottish league titles at Celtic under Martin O'Neill before following his manager to Villa Park in 2006.
Captained Aston Villa to three consecutive sixth-place finishes and a League Cup final; scored an iconic 47-yard volley against Derby County in 2008.
Wore shirt #19, nicknamed 'Stan', celebrated for inspirational leadership and honored by fans with a 19th-minute standing ovation after battling leukemia.
Iconic / Primary Club: Aston Villa

name: Nolberto Solano
bonusClues: Played alongside Diego Maradona at Boca Juniors, who affectionately nicknamed him 'El Maestrito' (The Little Master).
Became the first Peruvian in Premier League history in 1998, racking up 49 goals and 62 assists across two spells on Tyneside.
Wore shirt #4 (and #7), famous for inch-perfect crosses onto Alan Shearer's head and playing the trumpet in a salsa band.
Iconic / Primary Club: Newcastle United

name: Kevin Phillips
bonusClues: Worked in a supermarket and played semi-pro non-league football for Baldock Town as a right-back before converting to striker at Watford.
Scored 30 Premier League goals in 1999-2000 to win the European Golden Shoe—remains the only Englishman in history to win it.
Wore shirt #10, celebrated for telepathic 'little and large' strike partnership with 6ft 4in Niall Quinn at the Stadium of Light.
Iconic / Primary Club: Sunderland

name: Shola Ameobi
bonusClues: Moved to Newcastle from Nigeria as a young boy, coming through the club's youth academy to make his debut against Chelsea in 2000.
Spent 14 seasons at Newcastle, scoring 79 goals and earning cult status by scoring 7 times against arch-rivals Sunderland.
Wore shirt #23, affectionately nicknamed 'The Mackem Slayer', legendary for having one of the highest penalty conversion rates in Premier League history.
Iconic / Primary Club: Newcastle United

name: Brede Hangeland
bonusClues: Born in Houston, Texas, but raised in Stavanger, Norway, he played for Viking and Copenhagen before Roy Hodgson signed him for Fulham in 2008.
Captained Fulham to the 2010 UEFA Europa League final and formed one of the Premier League's sturdiest defensive walls.
Wore shirt #5, towering 6ft 6in cultured centre-back known for calm clean tackling, gentlemanly sportsmanship, and set-piece headers.
Iconic / Primary Club: Fulham

name: Jussi Jääskeläinen
bonusClues: Signed for Bolton from VPS Vaasa in 1997 for just £100,000, going on to spend 15 years and make over 500 appearances for the Trotters.
Famously saved two penalties in the same match against Blackburn Rovers in 2006 to preserve a historic 1-0 victory.
Wore shirt #22, beloved for cat-like double reflexive saves from point-blank range and his iconic Finnish stoicism.
Iconic / Primary Club: Bolton Wanderers

name: Thomas Sørensen
bonusClues: Signed by Peter Reid at Sunderland as Peter Schmeichel's national team successor before starring for Aston Villa and Stoke City.
Saved penalty kicks from Alan Shearer, Thierry Henry, and Cristiano Ronaldo across a distinguished 364-game Premier League career.
Wore shirt #29 (and #1), legendary shot-stopper who anchored the Britannia Stadium fortress under Tony Pulis.
Iconic / Primary Club: Stoke City

name: Sylvain Distin
bonusClues: Arrived in England with Newcastle United on loan from PSG before becoming a defensive pillar for Man City, Portsmouth, and Everton.
Holds the Premier League record for the most appearances by an overseas outfield player with 469 appearances.
Wore shirt #15, an athletic physical specimen blessed with incredible recovery pace and supreme longevity into his late thirties.
Iconic / Primary Club: Everton

name: Charlie Adam
bonusClues: Rangers youth product who spearheaded Ian Holloway's fearless Blackpool side to Championship promotion in 2010.
Scored from a mind-blowing 66 yards inside his own half against Thibaut Courtois at Stamford Bridge in 2015.
Wore shirt #26, famous for his cultured left foot, booming cross-field Hollywood passes, and dangerous curling in-swinging corners.
Iconic / Primary Club: Blackpool

name: Grant Holt
bonusClues: Worked as a tyre fitter while playing non-league football for Workington, Halifax, and Barrow before climbing every tier of English football.
Scored 15 Premier League goals in 2011-12 for newly promoted Norwich City, finishing as the second-highest English scorer in the league.
Wore shirt #9, a throwback bruising physical target man who bullied centre-backs with brute strength and aerial dominance.
Iconic / Primary Club: Norwich City

name: Duncan Ferguson
bonusClues: Signed from Rangers in 1994, becoming an instant Goodison Park cult deity when he scored in a Merseyside derby win over Liverpool.
Scored 68 Premier League goals for Everton and won the 1995 FA Cup, famously serving as caretaker manager with passionate sideline theatrics.
Wore shirt #9, nicknamed 'Big Dunc', notorious for his terrifying physical aggression, blue sweatband on his wrist, and towering headers.
Iconic / Primary Club: Everton

name: Juninho Paulista
bonusClues: Sensational coup signing from São Paulo in 1995 that stunned English football, arriving in the icy northeast of England as a Brazilian superstar.
Had three separate spells on Teesside, winning the 2004 League Cup and crying on the pitch after relegation in 1997.
Wore shirt #10, nicknamed 'The Little Fella' (standing just 5ft 5in), revered for jinking hips, dribbling acceleration, and heart on his sleeve.
Iconic / Primary Club: Middlesbrough

name: Fabricio Coloccini
bonusClues: Developed at Boca Juniors and AC Milan before establishing himself in La Liga with Deportivo La Coruña.
Captained Newcastle to a stunning fifth-place finish in 2011-12 and was named in the PFA Premier League Team of the Year.
Wears shirt #2, iconic Argentine defender with glorious curly locks, serenaded by the Toon Army with 'he wears a perm, he wears a perm'.
Iconic / Primary Club: Newcastle United

name: Mark Viduka
bonusClues: Hailed from Melbourne Knights and Dinamo Zagreb before becoming Scottish Player of the Year at Celtic.
Scored all four goals in an unforgettable 4-3 victory over Liverpool at Elland Road in November 2000.
Wore shirt #9, renowned for extraordinary back-to-goal hold-up play, pirouettes in the box, and delicate outside-of-the-boot touches.
Iconic / Primary Club: Leeds United

name: Jon Walters
bonusClues: Began at Blackburn and Bolton before dropping into the lower leagues with Hull, Chester, and Ipswich Town.
The tireless workhorse engine of Tony Pulis's Stoke side, helping them reach the 2011 FA Cup final and the Europa League.
Wore shirt #19, famous for never-ending running, physical combat against defenders, and once scoring two own-goals and missing a penalty in a single match.
Iconic / Primary Club: Stoke City

name: Ryan Shawcross
bonusClues: Manchester United academy graduate who joined Stoke City initially on loan in 2007 before captaining them for a decade.
Made over 400 appearances for Stoke, anchoring one of the most physically intimidating backlines in Premier League history.
Wore shirt #17, long-serving captain feared for uncompromising tough-tackling, blood-and-guts defending, and set-piece headers.
Iconic / Primary Club: Stoke City

name: Christopher Samba
bonusClues: Signed from Hertha BSC for just £450,000 after a successful trial under Mark Hughes at Ewood Park.
Anchor of Blackburn's defense for five years, famously utilized as an emergency striker by Sam Allardyce due to his aerial power.
Wore shirt #4, towering 6ft 4in brick-wall defender famous for bullet headers, crunching recovery slide challenges, and brute strength.
Iconic / Primary Club: Blackburn Rovers

name: Amr Zaki
bonusClues: Signed on loan from Zamalek in 2008 by Steve Bruce after firing Egypt to the 2008 Africa Cup of Nations title.
Exploded with 10 Premier League goals in his first 16 games, briefly sitting as the Premier League top scorer ahead of Rooney and Ronaldo.
Wore shirt #9, nicknamed 'The Bulldozer', immortalized by a stunning scissor-kick volley at Anfield before disappearing after going AWOL.
Iconic / Primary Club: Wigan Athletic
